extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and publication criteria for manuscripts submitted to the open-access journal PLOS ONE, specifying what article types are acceptable and the scientific, ethical, reporting, and presentation standards required for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of primary scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate primary scientific research in any applied discipline that contributes to the base of scientific knowledge. The journal will not consider reviews, case studies, study protocols, hypothesis/proposal papers, letters/commentaries/essays, opinion pieces, policy papers, other secondary literature, monographs, or purely theoretical research (such as pure mathematics). Occasionally commissioned Collection Reviews or Overviews are accepted only when solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative article types (with conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain non-primary-article types may be considered if they meet specific methodological or solicitation conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews are considered only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling of existing literature; submissions describing methods, software, databases, or other tools are considered if they follow appropriate reporting guidelines; qualitative research is considered only if it adheres to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines. See submission guidelines for discipline-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere; PLOS ONE does not accept studies already published in whole or in part in peer-reviewed literature or submissions under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All manuscript figures must be original and not previously published. However, manuscripts deposited in preprint servers (e.g., arXiv), published in a thesis, or presented at conferences may be considered. Authors must not submit work under simultaneous consideration at other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and derivative studies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted study replicates or is very similar to previous work, authors must provide a sound scientific rationale and clearly reference and discuss the existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that are replication or derivative of existing work will likely be rejected if authors do not provide adequate justification and contextualization against prior studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rigor of experiments, statistics, and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses must be performed to a high technical standard and described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must be conducted rigorously with appropriate controls and replication; sample sizes must be large enough to produce robust results where applicable; methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions must be presented appropriately and be supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will be rejected if interpretation is unjustified or inappropriate; authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Authors may discuss possible implications but must clearly label such discussion as hypotheses rather than conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article must be presented in an intelligible fashion and written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts, so language must be clear, correct, and unambiguous. Papers with unclear language or many errors may be rejected or authors may be advised to seek independent editorial/manuscript editing services prior to revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics of experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The research must meet all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research must be conducted to the highest ethical standards; PLOS ONE may have standards more stringent than local requirements. Approval from relevant bodies is required for studies involving humans (including observational/survey/personal data), animals (including observational studies), non-commercial cell lines, field sampling, and potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why. Contact plosone@plos.org for questions on compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication ethics and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to comply with best practices in publication ethics per COPE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE is a COPE member and follows COPE Code of Conduct and Best Practice Guidelines. Authors must adhere to best practices regarding authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. Concerns should be addressed to the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must adhere to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for results reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results must be rigorously reported appropriate to community standards; see submission guidelines for discipline-specific reporting checklists and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The article must adhere to community standards for data availability and deposition in publicly available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow standards for data deposition (e.g., gene sequences, microarray expression, structural studies). Failure to comply with community data-sharing standards may result in rejection. See PLOS ONE data availability policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure originality
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures included in manuscripts should be original and should not have been published in any previous publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures previously published elsewhere may lead to rejection; ensure figure originality or provide appropriate justification/permissions if necessary.
